review_notes: Commons/Nature Communications foam-evolution video shows many small gas domains progressively disappearing while larger domains remain, grow, and reorganize. A single frame only shows a foam pattern; the named concept requires observing coarsening over time. The opening title card was removed and metadata/audio were stripped.

The clip mainly shows an insect interacting with a liquid surface. It does not make elastic stretching followed by restoring recoil visually decisive, so accepting Viscoelastic Recoil would rely on source context rather than video evidence.

The opening title leaks vitrimer/heat-gun processing context, and the visible sequence is a material-processing fixture experiment. The video does not independently show a clear stretch-release-recoil cycle required for Viscoelastic Recoil.

The clip is a warning-map/satellite overlay animation with place labels and advisory polygons. It does not show raw storm-surge inundation or water-front propagation, so the task would become map interpretation rather than video-native dynamic concept recognition.

The GIF cleanly illustrates wavefront bending across regions with different propagation speeds, but this concept is currently extension-tier because available footage is a teaching/simulation animation. Hold out of the v1 main quota unless an educational-simulation slice is explicitly added.
